comment: The short cut for the post on X. Scenes in order: a slide (hook, close) with its seconds, or a window of a capture segment (seg, from and to in the segment's play seconds, see data.ts; to null is the segment's end). Narration: one line per recorded clip, `at` in seconds from the start of its scene; `say` is what the voice reads when it differs from the subtitle `text`. voice.cjs reads this file too.

narration.text: Companies pay fake invoices because whoever pays can be fooled. In Bursar, the AI only reads. The company's NEAR contract decides.
An invoice arrives. It is read inside a NEAR AI Cloud enclave, which attests itself and signs what it read. The signature is verified right here, in the page.
The agent's key can only ask. The contract checks vendor, payout, caps and orders, and pays in the same transaction. Nobody had to look.
Next invoice, same vendor, with a note: please use our new bank details. The classic fraud. Will the contract notice?
Blocked. That payout is not the one the owner registered. No money moved.
A law firm's invoice: 9,800 USDC. That is above the threshold the owner set, so the contract will not pay it on its own.
narration.say: A law firm's invoice: nine thousand eight hundred USDC. That is above the threshold the owner set, so the contract will not pay it on its own.

narration.text: Held for a person. The owner approves with their own key, and only then it is paid. The approval is on chain too.
This vendor is paid on Base, another chain. Same reading, same checks.
Queued. On mainnet, NEAR Intents settles it on a quote the contract verifies.
Every reading leaves a receipt anyone can check, right in the browser.
Change a single byte, and the signature fails.
Bursar. The AI reads. The contract decides. A dumb executor moves the money. Proven on NEAR mainnet with real USDC. Try it at bursar.network.
narration.say: Bursar. The AI reads. The contract decides. A dumb executor moves the money. Proven on NEAR mainnet with real USDC. Try it at bursar dot network.
